name: Island Peak Climbing
alt_names: Island Peak with Everest Base Camp
sub_region: Solukhumbu District, Koshi Province (Imja valley, Sagarmatha National Park)

difficulty.notes: Glacier travel roped, possible crevasse ladders, a 100-200 m snow/ice headwall of about 40-50 degrees climbed on fixed rope with ascender (jumar), then a short exposed summit ridge; abseil descent. Summit day 10-15 h with a 1-3 am start. Crampon, ice-axe and fixed-rope skills are taught at base camp.

duration_days.basis: Full trip Kathmandu-Kathmandu, combined with Everest Base Camp and Kala Patthar
duration_days.notes: Operators sell 18-day (from Lukla) EBC + Island Peak packages and 14-16 day standalone versions via Chhukung. Short 5-day climbs start from Chhukung for already-acclimatised trekkers. Some teams use a high camp (about 5,600 m); others summit from base camp. Extended versions add Gokyo and Cho La (22-25 days).

start_point: Kathmandu (fly to Lukla, or via Manthali/Ramechhap in peak seasons)

itinerary.route: Acclimatisation day: Hotel Everest View / Khumjung
Lobuche - Gorak Shep - Everest Base Camp - Gorak Shep
Chhukung - Island Peak Base Camp (Pareshaya Gyab)
Base camp: rope, crampon and jumar training
itinerary.notes: Some teams move to High Camp (about 5,600 m) instead.

itinerary.route: Summit Island Peak - return to Chhukung
itinerary.notes: Rock gully, crampon point (about 5,800 m), glacier, headwall, summit ridge.

best_seasons.notes: NMA royalty is lower in autumn (USD 175) than spring (USD 350).

permits.name: NMA climbing permit (royalty) - Imja Tse (Island Peak)
permits.fee: USD 350 per person spring (Mar-May); USD 175 autumn (Sep-Nov), winter (Dec-Feb) and summer (Jun-Aug)
permits.valid_from: 2025-09-01 (flat per-person rate replaced old group-size tiers)

permits.name: Garbage deposit (refundable, per team)
permits.fee: USD 500 per team (NMA FAQ: all 27 NMA peaks; matches DoT schedule for peaks below 6,500 m in Khumbu)

permits.name: Sagarmatha National Park entry permit
permits.fee: NPR 3,000 per person per entry (SAARC NPR 1,500)

permits.name: Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality Trek-Card
permits.fee: NPR 3,000 per person (SAARC and Chinese nationals NPR 2,000)

guide_requirements: NMA peak permits are issued only through a registered Nepali agency, and every climbing party must be accompanied by an NMA-registered guide/sirdar (operator summaries of NMA rules; the 2025 Sixth Amendment to the Mountaineering Regulation also requires at least one mountain guide per team on peaks below 8,000 m). The trekking approach falls under the Khumbu guide-rule dispute (NTB lists Everest routes; the municipality does not enforce it).

flights: Peak-season diversion via Manthali (Ramechhap): roughly spring Chaitra-Jestha and autumn first week of Ashwin to 15 Mangsir
drives: Kathmandu - Manthali about 4-5 h when Lukla flights are diverted
logistics.notes: Teahouses on the approach; tents at base camp (and high camp if used). Climbing Sherpas fix ropes on the headwall.

highlights: Summit of Imja Tse (Island Peak) between Lhotse and Ama Dablam
Everest Base Camp and Kala Patthar on the acclimatisation trek
Imja Glacier and the headwall on fixed rope
Close views of the Lhotse south face
First climbed in 1956 (Swiss-Nepali); its SW summit was reached in 1953 by the British Everest expedition (Himalayan Database)
risks: Crevasses on the Imja Glacier (ladder crossings)
Fatigue on a 10-15 h summit day

acclimatization.notes: The EBC/Kala Patthar loop provides several nights near 5,000 m before the climb.

secondary_keywords: Island Peak with Everest Base Camp

unverified: Summit height: Himalayan Database and NMA service-charge table give 6,165 m (used here); NMA peak list says 6,160 m; many operators use 6,189 m (an older map figure noted by the Himalayan Database).
Base camp height 5,087 m vs 5,150 m and high camp about 5,600 m are operator figures.
Headwall length (100-200 m) and angle (40-50 degrees) vary by operator and season.
NMA-registered guide/sirdar requirement is from operator summaries of NMA rules, not read directly on an NMA page in this research.
